Practical.title: SQL — Practical
Practical.body:
Q: What is the difference between == and .equals()?
Ans • The == operator compares the memory address (reference), whereas the .equals() method compares the actual content or state of the objects.

Q: What is the Java Collections Framework?
Ans • It is a unified architecture for storing and manipulating a group of objects, providing readymade interfaces like List, Set, and Map.

Q: What is the 'this' keyword in Java?
Ans • The this keyword is a reference variable that refers to the current object, commonly used to resolve ambiguity between instance variables and parameters.

Q: What is the purpose of the 'super' keyword?
Ans • The super keyword is used to refer to immediate parent class objects, allowing access to parent methods, constructors, and variables.

Q: What is Garbage Collection in Java?
Ans • It is an automatic process where the JVM identifies and deletes unused objects from memory to reclaim space, so the programmer doesn't have to manually manage memory.

Q: What is a Wrapper Class?
Ans • Wrapper classes provide a way to use primitive data types (like int, char) as objects (like Integer, Character), which is necessary for many Collection classes.
